Step 1 · Predict: find what is missing

This component listens for changes in the window size. You hide it and change the size again. What happens in the console?

src/WindowSize.jsx
  1. import { useEffect } from 'react';
  3. export default function WindowSize() {
  4. useEffect(() => {
  5. const handleResize = () => console.log('resize');
  6. window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
  7. }, []);
  9. return <p>Change the size of the window.</p>;
  10. }
Incorrect. That happens only if the effect returns a function that removes the listener.
Correct. With no cleanup, the two StrictMode listeners stay alive after unmount.
Incorrect. StrictMode mounted twice and added two listeners.

Step 1 · Predict: find what is missing

What is missing?

src/WindowSize.jsx
  1. import { useEffect } from 'react';
  3. export default function WindowSize() {
  4. useEffect(() => {
  5. const handleResize = () => console.log('resize');
  6. window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
  7. }, []);
  9. return <p>Change the size of the window.</p>;
  10. }
Incorrect. It would remove it at once: the component would never listen to anything.
Incorrect. handleResize exists only inside the effect. In the array it gives the error "handleResize is not defined" and the page breaks.
Correct.

Step 3 · Compare

How did your clock advance?

Incorrect. Two intervals are alive: the cleanup is missing.
Correct. Only one interval alive.
Incorrect. Use setSeconds((s) => s + 1): with seconds + 1, the interval remembers the 0.
Incorrect. Did you put seconds in the array with no cleanup? Every second a new interval is born.

Step 3 · Compare

One possible solution

  1. import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
  3. export default function Timer() {
  4. const [seconds, setSeconds] = useState(0);
  6. useEffect(() => {
  7. console.log('Timer started');
  8. const id = setInterval(() => {
  9. setSeconds((s) => s + 1);
  10. }, 1000);
  11. return () => {
  12. clearInterval(id);
  13. console.log('Timer stopped');
  14. };
  15. }, []);
  17. return <p>{seconds}</p>;
  18. }
  1. import { useState } from 'react';
  2. import Timer from './Timer';
  4. export default function App() {
  5. const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(true);
  7. return (
  8. <div>
  9. <button onClick={() => setIsVisible(!isVisible)}>
  10. {isVisible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}
  11. </button>
  12. {isVisible && <Timer />}
  13. </div>
  14. );
  15. }

Step 3 · Compare

In short

  • If an effect starts something, its cleanup stops it.
  • React cleans up before repeating the effect, on unmount and, in development, on every test mount.
  • Inside an interval, use the function form s => s + 1.
